questions.question: What is a habitat? Give one example of a big habitat and one of a small habitat.
questions.expected_answer: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives and gets the food, water, shelter and space it needs. A big habitat is a grassland, forest or the sea; a small habitat is the space under a rock or a rotting log.

questions.question: Compare a grassland habitat with a forest habitat.
questions.expected_answer: A grassland is wide and open with mostly grass and very few trees, with grazers like zebra and blesbok. A forest has many tall trees close together, making it shady, cool and damp, with animals like the Knysna turaco and blue duiker.

questions.question: How is a river habitat different from a sea habitat? Name two animals for each.
questions.expected_answer: A river has fresh, flowing water, while the sea has salty water. River animals include fish, frogs, hippos and crocodiles. Sea animals include dolphins, whales, sharks, seals, crabs and sardines.
